dedication.title: For Lúcia
dedication.etym: From Latin Lucia, feminine of Lucius, derived from lux, lucis: “light”.
senses: The luminous one; she who brings light.
According to tradition, a name given in ancient Rome to children born at dawn.
In this project: the grandmother to whom this library is dedicated.
dedication.related: From the same root: lucid, elucidate, illuminate.
text: This project bears the name of Lúcia, the grandmother of the person who created it.
She is no longer here, but the name remained, and with it what such a name promises: light.
Every library is a way of turning on the light for someone. May everyone who learns something here carry a little of that brightness forward.

support.title: Support Instituto Lúcia
support.lead: The library is free and has no ads, and it will stay that way, with or without your contribution.
paragraphs: Instituto Lúcia has no sponsor, sells no courses and does not sell your data. It is kept going by volunteer work, because knowledge is not a commodity.

Even so, keeping a site online costs money. Those who can help pay that bill guarantee access for those who cannot. That is how the working class has always built what is its own: by pooling the little each one has.
The money raised has a clear destination:
costs: Domain and hosting for the site.
Storage for audio and for backup copies of the collection.
Whatever is left goes into expanding the collection: more lessons, more translations, more reviewing.
support.optional: Donating is entirely optional. Nobody loses access to anything for not contributing, and there is no exclusive content for donors. If money is tight, do not donate: study, share a lesson or come and volunteer. That sustains the project too.
support.note: Contributions are made on Benfeitoria, a Brazilian crowdfunding platform. This site neither receives nor stores payment data.
support.wallLead: Those who helped keep the institute standing and chose to leave their name here.

mural.title: Workers' Wall
mural.lead: Looking for a laundress, a bricklayer, a seamstress, a cooperative? Choose the state and the city. Self-employed? Post an ad: it is free, with no middleman and no fee.
mural.description: A free space for working people to publicise cooperatives, services, products, art and initiatives.
rules: It is for those who live from their own work: cooperatives, associations, self-employed workers, artisans, artists, collectives and community initiatives.
Not accepted: companies looking for labour, catalogue reselling, pyramid schemes, loans, betting, promises of easy money and election advertising.
No account is needed to post. Every ad is read by the coordination before it goes up and stays visible for 180 days. City and state are required.
The contact details you write are public. Post only what anyone may see.
The institute charges nothing, takes no share of any sale and does not vouch for the services listed. Seen something wrong? Use the Report link.

news.title: News from Brazil
news.lead: The latest headlines from Brazil's grassroots, independent and public press, gathered in one place. Tap a headline to read the story on the publisher's own site. The headlines are in Portuguese.
news.description: Recent headlines from Brazil's grassroots, independent and public press, updated every fifteen minutes.
news.updated: Updated at {time} (Brasília time); the list refreshes every fifteen minutes
news.empty: The headlines could not be fetched right now. Try again in a few minutes.
news.note: The institute does not write, edit or answer for these texts: it shows only the title, date and link that each outlet distributes publicly. The institute's own stories are in the Journal.

gallery.eyebrow: Art and press of the struggle
gallery.title: Poster gallery
gallery.lead: Before radio and television, the wall was the newspaper of working people. These posters, prints and photographs were made to call, to teach and to denounce. Each one comes with who made it, when and why.
gallery.description: Historical posters, prints and photographs of the workers' struggle, in the public domain, with context and source.
gallery.note: Only public domain works are shown here, stored on this site with their source. A poster is a document of its time: showing it is not endorsing everything that was done in its name.
